newsitem.title: USA: Cowboys star Erik Williams sues police, TV station.
newsitem.headline: Cowboys star Erik Williams sues police, TV station.

text.p: Dallas Cowboys star Erik Williams has filed a lawsuit against Dallas police and a television station for allegedly violating his rights in their handling of a sex assault allegation against him and a teammate, his lawyer said on Wednesday.

Williams' attorney Peter Ginsberg said he filed a federal court lawsuit against the City of Dallas and five Dallas police officers, as well as a state court defamation lawsuit against KXAS-TV and its reporter Marty Griffin.
"It is a civil rights action accusing city officials of violating Erik's civil rights in a variety of very significant ways," Ginsberg said.

Local television reports said Williams, a star offensive lineman, planned to donate whatever damages he receives from the lawsuits to charity. Williams and teammate Michael Irvin were accused of sexually assaulting a 23-year-old Dallas woman, Nina Shahravan, at gunpoint on Dec. 29.
Dallas police announced details of the investigation before charging either player and after a highly-publicised 11-day probe, concluded that the woman had invented the false allegations.
Shahravan was then charged with perjury but she insists she was raped at Williams' home.
Ginsberg said the police and KXAS had jumped too fast to accuse Irvin and Williams of carrying out the alleged rape.

"They dealt with Erik and Michael differently because they are black, because they are rich and successful. Certain members of the police do not like them or the way they live," Ginsberg said on Wednesday.
He said KXAS and Griffin were aware of credibility problems with Shahravan from the start but focused only on details of the case that suggested the men were guilty.

An attorney for the television station said it had full confidence in Griffin's reporting of the case and would fight back. "We are going to vigorously defend the station and aggressively investigate Mr. Williams' conduct and his background," lawyer Chip Babcock said. "At the end of the day, we think we will be exonerated."
Dallas police declined to comment on the lawsuit.
A lawyer for Irvin said the star wide receiver had not yet decided whether to join Williams in suing police or any media organisation.
